findings.title: Make() with EnableSmartTruncate=false and default MaxLength=0 returns empty slug
findings.property: With MaxLength unset (0), slugs are not shortened, so a simple lowercase word is returned unchanged regardless of EnableSmartTruncate
findings.evidence: Doc on MaxLength: 'By default slugs aren't shortened.' The non-smart branch `len(slug) >= MaxLength` does not guard MaxLength > 0 (unlike the smart branch).

error.message: Make("a") with MaxLength=0 and smart truncate off = "", want "a"

review.title: MakeLang returns an empty slug when EnableSmartTruncate=false and MaxLength is 0 (the default)
review.reason: slug.go:131 runs `if !EnableSmartTruncate && len(slug) >= MaxLength { slug = slug[:MaxLength] }` with no `MaxLength > 0` check. With the default MaxLength=0, `len(slug) >= 0` is always true, so every slug is cut to `slug[:0]` and comes back empty. The MaxLength doc says 'By default slugs aren't shortened', and the smart branch at line 144 guards with `MaxLength > 0`, so the missing guard is an oversight and not intended. The repro uses the public API correctly, and a one-line fix is trivial for a maintainer to accept.

findings.title: Make() with MaxLength can return slug ending in underscore, failing IsSlug
findings.property: All output of Make(text) passes IsSlug (when non-empty)
findings.expected: a slug without trailing '_' (e.g. "0") that passes IsSlug
findings.evidence: IsSlug doc: 'All output from slug.Make(text) should pass this test' and slugs may not end with '-' or '_'. smartTruncate cuts text[:MaxLength] without re-trimming '_' / '-'.

error.message: Make("0_0") with MaxLength=2 = "0_", not a valid slug

review.title: Make() with MaxLength can return a slug ending in '_' that fails IsSlug
review.reason: The IsSlug doc says all output from Make should pass it, and IsSlug rejects a trailing '_' or '-'. With smart truncation, Make trims the ends first and then calls smartTruncate. smartTruncate cuts at `text[:MaxLength]`, or at the last '-', without re-trimming. So "0_0" with MaxLength=2 becomes "0_", and a cut at a '-' can leave a trailing '_' in the same way. The input is ordinary, the guarantee is documented, and re-trimming `-_` after truncation is a small fix a maintainer would accept.
